requirements.title: Credential presentation
requirements.rationale: Every later route trusts what authentication reports about the caller, so the three credential types and the two public routes are fixed once.

criteria.condition: a request to a non-public route under /api/v1 carries an Authorization header with the scheme Bearer, in any letter case, and a live admin token, API key or PAT
criteria.action: pass the request to the next check and report the caller to it: the credential type, the credential id, the user with role and status (none for the admin token) and, for a PAT, its permissions, paths and workspace
criteria.contract: the route's handler runs and reads a caller {type: "admin" | "api_key" | "pat", credential_id: "admin" | key_id | token_id, user: User or none, permissions: string[], paths: string[] or null, workspace: string or null}; permissions, paths and workspace are set only for a PAT

setup: a test hub: the request pipeline of internal/server with the authenticator and routes of internal/identity installed, over a store opened in t.TempDir()
the store is bootstrapped with an admin token through the bootstrap code of package 03
user alice (role user, status active) holds a live API key and a live PAT with permissions [git:read], paths [docs/**] and no workspace
a non-public test route GET /api/v1/test/whoami that answers 200 with the caller it was given
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/authenticate_test.go, a table over {admin token, API key, PAT} x scheme {Bearer, bearer, BEARER}: r = get('/api/v1/test/whoami', Authorization: scheme + ' ' + credential); assert r.status == 200; admin: assert r.json.type == 'admin' and r.json.credential_id == 'admin' and r.json.user == null; API key: assert type == 'api_key' and credential_id == key_id and user.id == alice.id and user.role == 'user' and user.status == 'active'; PAT: assert type == 'pat' and credential_id == token_id and user.id == alice.id and permissions == ['git:read'] and paths == ['docs/**'] and workspace == null; one more row with two spaces after the scheme and a trailing space after the credential: assert 200

criteria.condition: a request to a non-public route under /api/v1 has no Authorization header, a scheme other than Bearer, an empty credential, or a credential that matches none of the three wire formats
criteria.action: refuse the request before any later check runs
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated and message "authentication required"; the route's handler does not run

criteria.condition: the credential matches a wire format and its id is not stored, or its secret does not match the stored hash, or it has the admin format and differs from the admin token or the hub is not bootstrapped
criteria.action: refuse the request without saying which of the id and the secret was wrong
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated and message "invalid credentials"; the body is the same for an unknown id and for a wrong secret

criteria.condition: a request to GET /auth/providers or POST /auth/callback carries no Authorization header, or one that would fail authentication on another route
criteria.action: answer the route without authenticating the request
criteria.contract: the same status and body as the same request without the header; GET /api/v1/auth/providers answers 200

requirements.title: Credential state
requirements.rationale: A revoked, expired or blocked credential must stop working at once, and its state must not be readable by someone who holds only its id.

criteria.condition: the secret of an API key or PAT matches and the credential's revoked_at is set
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated and message "credential revoked"

user alice holds a live API key and a live PAT

check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/authenticate_test.go, a table over {API key, PAT}: assert get('/api/v1/test/whoami', bearer).status == 200; set revoked_at = now in the store; r = get('/api/v1/test/whoami', bearer); assert r.status == 401; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'unauthenticated'; assert r.json.error.message == 'credential revoked'

criteria.condition: the secret of an API key or PAT matches, the credential is not revoked and the current time is at or after its expires_at
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated and message "credential expired"; a credential whose expires_at is null or later than the current time passes

criteria.condition: the secret of an API key or PAT matches, the credential is neither revoked nor expired and its user's status is blocked
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden and message "user is blocked"; the credential's record is unchanged

criteria.action: for any credential that fails more than one check, give the answer of the first failing check in the order format, secret, revoked, expired, blocked, so that a wrong secret is always answered "invalid credentials" whatever the credential's state
criteria.contract: revoked and expired: 401 "credential revoked"; revoked with a blocked user: 401 "credential revoked"; expired with a blocked user: 401 "credential expired"; the id of a revoked, expired or blocked user's credential with a wrong secret: 401 "invalid credentials" with the same body as an unknown id

criteria.condition: a blocked user's status returns to active
criteria.action: authenticate again every credential of that user that is neither revoked nor expired, and keep refusing the revoked and the expired ones
criteria.contract: the live API key and the live PAT are answered 200; the revoked key is answered 401 "credential revoked"; the expired PAT is answered 401 "credential expired"

requirements.title: Provider list
requirements.rationale: A client that starts a login has to learn where to send the browser without holding a credential or a client secret.

criteria.condition: a caller sends GET /auth/providers
criteria.action: answer the configured providers ordered by name, each with its name and an authorize_url that carries the provider's client id and the scopes the hub needs: user:email for github, openid email profile for google
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 {items: [{name: string, authorize_url: string}], next_cursor: null} with Cache-Control: public, max-age=300; github: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=<client_id>&scope=user%3Aemail; google: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with the query parameters client_id, scope "openid email profile" and response_type "code"; an item has no other member

setup: a test hub: the request pipeline of internal/server with the authenticator and routes of internal/identity installed, over a store opened in t.TempDir()
the configuration lists google (client_id gg-id, client_secret gg-secret) before github (client_id gh-id, client_secret gh-secret), with no URL overrides
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/providers_test.go: r = get('/api/v1/auth/providers'); assert r.status == 200; assert r.header['Cache-Control'] == 'public, max-age=300'; assert r.json.next_cursor == null; assert names(r.json.items) == ['github', 'google']; assert r.json.items[0].authorize_url == 'https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=gh-id&scope=user%3Aemail'; u = parse(r.json.items[1].authorize_url); assert u.scheme + '://' + u.host + u.path == 'https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth'; assert u.query == {client_id: 'gg-id', scope: 'openid email profile', response_type: 'code'}; assert keys(each item) == {name, authorize_url}; assert not contains(r.body, 'gh-secret') and not contains(r.body, 'gg-secret') and no response header contains either

criteria.action: answer GET /auth/providers with an empty list
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 {items: [], next_cursor: null}

criteria.action: for any answer of GET /auth/providers, leave every configured client_secret out of the body and the headers

requirements.title: Identity read from the provider
requirements.rationale: The hub knows a person only through the stable id and the verified e-mail the provider vouches for.

criteria.condition: a login with provider github holds a code and an allowed redirect_uri
criteria.action: exchange the code at the provider's token URL for an access token and read the user's id, login, name and e-mail from the user URL with that token
criteria.contract: one form-encoded POST to the token URL with client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri and grant_type=authorization_code and the header Accept: application/json; one GET to the user URL with Authorization: Bearer <access token>; the identity is {provider: "github", provider_id: the id as a decimal string, username: login, full_name: name or "", email: the profile's email}

setup: a fake provider: an httptest server that answers the token URL and the user URL (and, for GitHub, the e-mail list URL) from a script the test sets, and records every request it receives
github is configured with client_id gh-id, client_secret gh-secret and token_url and userinfo_url pointing at the fake provider
the fake answers the token URL with {access_token: 'at-1'} and the user URL with {id: 123, login: 'alice', name: 'Alice A', email: 'a@x'}
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/oauth_test.go: id, err = client.Identity(ctx, 'github', 'code-1', 'http://127.0.0.1:5000/callback'); assert err == nil; assert id == {provider: 'github', provider_id: '123', username: 'alice', full_name: 'Alice A', email: 'a@x'}; t = fake.requests[0]; assert t.method == 'POST' and t.header['Accept'] == 'application/json' and t.form == {client_id: 'gh-id', client_secret: 'gh-secret', code: 'code-1', redirect_uri: 'http://127.0.0.1:5000/callback', grant_type: 'authorization_code'}; assert fake.requests[1].header['Authorization'] == 'Bearer at-1'; assert len(fake.requests) == 2

criteria.condition: the GitHub profile's email is null or empty
criteria.action: read the e-mail list from the user URL with /emails appended and use the address of the entry whose primary and verified are both true
criteria.contract: one GET to <user URL>/emails with Authorization: Bearer <access token>; identity.email is that entry's email

setup: a fake provider: an httptest server that answers the token URL and the user URL (and, for GitHub, the e-mail list URL) from a script the test sets, and records every request it receives
the fake answers the user URL with {id: 123, login: 'alice', email: null} and the e-mail list with [{email: 'old@x', primary: false, verified: true}, {email: 'a@x', primary: true, verified: true}]
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/oauth_test.go: id, err = client.Identity(ctx, 'github', 'code-1', uri); assert err == nil; assert id.email == 'a@x'; assert fake.requests[2].path ends with '/emails' and fake.requests[2].header['Authorization'] == 'Bearer at-1'

criteria.condition: a login with provider google holds a code and an allowed redirect_uri
criteria.action: exchange the code at the token URL and read sub, name, email and email_verified from the user URL
criteria.contract: the identity is {provider: "google", provider_id: sub, username: name, full_name: name, email: email}, and email is taken only when email_verified is true

criteria.condition: the provider gives no login or display name, or one that is empty after trimming white space
criteria.action: use <provider>-<provider_id> as the username
criteria.contract: identity.username is "github-123" for provider github with id 123, "google-1099" for provider google with sub 1099

criteria.condition: the provider's answer carries no user id, or no verified e-mail
criteria.action: fail the identity read as a failure of the provider and return no identity
criteria.contract: the identity read returns an error of the kind upstream, which POST /auth/callback answers as HTTP 502 with error_type upstream_error

setup: a fake provider: an httptest server that answers the token URL and the user URL (and, for GitHub, the e-mail list URL) from a script the test sets, and records every request it receives
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/oauth_test.go, a table over the fake's answers {github user without id, github email null with an e-mail list of [{primary: true, verified: false}, {primary: false, verified: true}], github email null with an empty e-mail list, google without sub, google with email_verified false, google with email_verified true and no email}: id, err = client.Identity(...); assert kind(err) == upstream; assert id is the zero value

criteria.condition: the token URL answers a JSON object with an error member and a status below 500
criteria.action: fail the identity read as a code the provider rejected, without calling the user URL
criteria.contract: the identity read returns an error of the kind rejected, which POST /auth/callback answers as HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated; the user URL receives no request

setup: a fake provider: an httptest server that answers the token URL and the user URL (and, for GitHub, the e-mail list URL) from a script the test sets, and records every request it receives
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/oauth_test.go, a table over the token answers {200 {error: 'bad_verification_code'}, 400 {error: 'invalid_grant'}}: id, err = client.Identity(...); assert kind(err) == rejected; assert len(fake.requests) == 1

criteria.condition: the token URL or the user URL cannot be reached, answers a status of 500 or above, answers a body that is not a JSON object, or the token URL answers neither an access token nor an error member, or the user URL answers a status other than 200
criteria.action: fail the identity read as a failure of the provider
criteria.contract: the identity read returns an error of the kind upstream; the error's text holds neither the code, the client secret, the access token nor the provider's body

setup: a fake provider: an httptest server that answers the token URL and the user URL (and, for GitHub, the e-mail list URL) from a script the test sets, and records every request it receives
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/oauth_test.go, a table over {token URL connection refused, token 503, token 200 'not json', token 200 {}, user URL 401, user URL 500, user URL 200 '[1,2]', e-mail list URL 500 when the profile hides the address}: id, err = client.Identity(ctx, 'github', 'code-1', uri); assert kind(err) == upstream; for each of 'code-1', 'gh-secret', 'at-1' and the fake's body text: assert not contains(err.Error(), it)

criteria.condition: a call to the provider has not answered within 15 seconds
criteria.action: abandon the call and fail the identity read as a failure of the provider
criteria.contract: the identity read returns an error of the kind upstream no later than the timeout plus the time of one scheduling delay; the connection to the provider is closed

requirements.title: First login
requirements.rationale: A person who signs in for the first time must leave with a user, an organization to own workspaces in and a working key, or with nothing at all.

criteria.condition: POST /auth/callback has read an identity whose provider and provider_id match no user
criteria.action: create, in one transaction, the user with status active, a personal org whose name is the username and whose owner_id is the user, the user's membership of that org and an API key, and answer the user and the key
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 {user: {id, username, email, full_name, role, status: "active", provider, provider_id, created_at, updated_at}, api_key: {key: "parley_<key_id>_<secret>", key_id, expires_at}}; the store then holds one user, one org with name == username and owner_id == user.id, one membership (org, user) and one live key; the returned key authenticates as that user

criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with user.username == the first free of <name>-2 … <name>-10; the personal org's name equals that username
